# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

## 1. Executive Summary

**Date of Agreement:** 2022-02-10

**Borrower/Company Overview:** SESI, L.L.C., a Delaware limited liability company, is the borrower under this credit facility. The parent company is SESI Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation. The borrower operates with multiple subsidiary guarantors including Superior Energy Services entities and various specialized service companies in the energy sector.

**Transaction Description:** This is a Third Amendment to an existing Credit Agreement originally dated February 2, 2021. The transaction involves SESI, L.L.C. as borrower, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. serving as administrative agent, along with multiple lenders including Bank of America, N.A. and Citibank, N.A. The amendment modifies certain provisions of the existing credit facility rather than establishing new financing.

**Purpose of Financing:** The purpose is to amend and modify certain terms of the existing Credit Agreement, specifically relating to asset disposition provisions and lien release mechanisms. The borrower requested these amendments to provide additional operational flexibility.

**Company Background:** Based on the subsidiary guarantor names, the company appears to operate in the energy services sector, with entities focused on drilling specialties, well control, inspection services, and energy equipment services across North America.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

**Key Strengths/Credit Positives:**
• Established banking relationships with high-quality financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., Bank of America, N.A., and Citibank, N.A.
• Borrower maintains minimum liquidity thresholds ($100,000,000) and availability requirements ($25,000,000) for certain disposition activities
• Asset disposition amendments provide operational flexibility while maintaining cash consideration requirements for borrowing base property sales
• Diversified subsidiary structure across multiple energy service verticals
• Automatic lien release provisions provide clear collateral management framework

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• Energy sector exposure subject to commodity price volatility and cyclical downturns
• Amendment suggests potential need for increased asset disposition flexibility, which may indicate operational or financial pressures
• Multiple previous amendments and waivers (First Amendment dated May 13, 2021, waivers dated May 28, 2021 and July 15, 2021, Second Amendment dated November 15, 2021) suggest ongoing covenant management issues
• Borrowing base structure indicates asset-based lending, suggesting potential concerns about cash flow coverage
